scope: Documented and tested backup, restore and disaster-recovery behaviour for SQLite and PostgreSQL. The portable Trestle logical archive is the cross-provider backup format; it never implies a backup of an operator's whole PostgreSQL cluster.

sqliteSnapshot.description: Native consistent SQLite snapshot (VACUUM INTO style) produced through the backup API.

portableArchive.description: Transactionally consistent Trestle logical archive (JSON) covering schema metadata, records, identities, rules, events, audit, jobs, integration targets and the file manifest, exported from one repeatable-read snapshot (PostgreSQL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY; SQLite shared lock).
portableArchive.restore: trestle restore --backup ARCHIVE --data-dir NEW_DATA_DIR | trestle restore --backup ARCHIVE --provider postgres --database-url URL

postgresDump.description: An operator-managed pg_dump or managed-cluster backup covers the whole PostgreSQL service and is a separate responsibility. Trestle does not produce it and never claims the portable archive replaces it.

restoreContract.destination: restore only into an initialized, logically empty destination. Every portable-owned table must be empty and system metadata must contain only the provider/initialization marker. The migration history must be current and authoritative.
restoreContract.atomicity: all-or-nothing transactional import; a failed restore leaves the destination semantically unchanged
restoreContract.preflight: hostile-archive preflight rejects missing manifest, future schema, unsafe names, symlinks, duplicates and unexpected entries before the destination is opened
restoreContract.secrets: webhook secrets are re-encrypted or disabled on restore; live sessions and bearer access tokens are revoked; credential secret hashes survive (lookup is hash-based)
restoreContract.files: the archive carries the file manifest; file bytes are backed up separately (local file tree or object storage); a file whose deletion was pending when the archive was taken is restored unavailable and its bytes cleaned by the deletion sweep

failureModes.corruptedArchive: rejected by preflight with actionable diagnostics
failureModes.futureSchema: rejected; the executable refuses a schema newer than it supports
failureModes.occupiedDestination: rejected; every portable-owned table must be empty
failureModes.wrongCredentials: connection failure is clean, bounded and never surfaces credentials
failureModes.failedUpgrade: migration failures roll back; the destination is left unchanged

verification.semanticDigest: cross-provider migration and restore verify a canonical content hash of the destination against the source, not row counts alone
verification.drill: scripts/test-restore-drill.sh runs a destructive backup, destroy, restore and verify round trip against isolated temporary data

operatorSteps.onlineBackup: use the authenticated backup API (or the portable export) while the deployment is running; the export is a repeatable-read snapshot
operatorSteps.restoreIntoEmpty: create an empty initialized destination, then run trestle restore with the archive and destination flags
operatorSteps.pgDump: operators of PostgreSQL may additionally schedule pg_dump/pg_basebackup or a managed-cluster backup; Trestle's portable archive is not a substitute
operatorSteps.rollback: executable rollback restores the previous binary; database downgrade is not automatic and is documented as unsupported

evidence.localRealService: portable round trips and restore drills on SQLite and real PostgreSQL 18.6
